A pending assignment has no subtitle - the name is in the README, which is embargoed until hand-out - so there the identifier is the heading, as it always was. {%- endcomment -%} {% if page.subtitle %}

{%- comment -%} `open_in.html` is the "open this in your local copy" strip: it reads the reader's profile and rewrites every repo shape on the page to their own. An `external` assignment has no repo at either level, so the strip offers to set up a local copy of nothing - and "set up" is the first thing on the page a student meets. {%- endcomment -%} {% unless page.submit_shape == "external" %} {% include open_in.html %} {% endunless %} {%- comment -%} Where the student actually works. This is the first thing they need and it used to be a grey italic line at the very bottom of the page, under the whole brief - so the answer to "where do I write this?" sat below the thing it was needed for. `repo_url` is the cohort org's repo list filtered to this assignment rather than one student's address: the page is public and identical for everyone, and GitHub shows a signed-in student only the repos they can see, so the filter lands on their own. Absent while the assignment is pending - there is nothing at the other end of it yet. {%- endcomment -%} {%- comment -%} `submit_shape` (site.py, off `course.submit_shape` and so off the assignment's own grading_config.yml) is the SHAPE in one word - `external`, `assignment-repo-private`, `assignment-repo-public`, `assignment-repo-student-choice`. `external` is handed in off GitHub - Moodle, Kaggle, in class - and NO repo is created for it at all. So there is nothing to open and nothing to name: the brief below says where the work goes, and `submit_url` puts a button on it when the assignment names an address. This block used to print off `repo_url` alone, so a Moodle assignment told the whole cohort that a push to `main` was its submission. `escape`: `repo_name` is a SHAPE, `-`, and those angle brackets make `` an unknown HTML tag that the browser silently drops - so the name rendered as `assignment-1-` with the useful half missing. `data-dsl-repo`: the repo SHAPE, and the one thing on the page that a reader with a profile can be told exactly. open_in.html rewrites every one of these to the real name (`assignment-1-jane`) and repoints every `data-dsl-repo-url` beside them at that repo, so a student stops reading `` and substituting themselves. Marked rather than matched on the prose, because the sentences around them are reworded. {%- endcomment -%} {%- comment -%} `handout_pending` gates the whole block: an assignment still to come has no brief to read and no address to go to, so a callout would answer a question the page has not asked yet. It is also why the external arm says only WHERE the work is handed in and never "no repository is created": a cohort handed out before that arm existed has the repos it was given, and this would be telling those students their own repo is not there. ONE arm for every shape that has a repo: one button, one link, and the `case` below branches only the SENTENCE. A shape that copied the button carried its own copy of the open_in.html contract to keep in step, and the two drifted the first time one of them was reworded. The callout answers ROUTE and nothing else - where the work goes, which of it is read, and what the deadline costs. Every shape's route is the same route: clone, commit, push to `main`. So the `case` is down to the two arms that genuinely differ - a shared drop box, where the address is a folder in one named repo, and `assignment-repo-public`, whose repo is not private and must not be called so. WHO CAN READ the repo is a different question, asked after the brief has been read rather than above it, and it is answered once, in the `shape_note` box at the foot of this page (`course.SHAPE_NOTES`). Where the marks land is not answered here at all. It was, on four of the five arms, in four wordings of one sentence - and the page a student opens to find out what to do is not where they go looking for a mark. The gradebook is `grades-`, it is the same repo for every shape, and it says so itself, on every row it carries. `repo_name_is_shape` (site.py) is what decides whether the two data attributes are written at all. `shared_dropbox_repo` is the one shape whose `repo_name` is a REAL repo and not a shape: there is a single private drop box for the whole cohort, and what is the student's own is a folder in it (`submit_path`). There is nothing in that name for open_in.html to substitute a handle into, and rewriting it would point every reader at a repo that does not exist - so the flag is false and the markers are left off. `data-dsl-dropbox` / `data-dsl-dropbox-path` are what that shape gets INSTEAD, on the callout itself: the real repo name handed over as a fact, and beside it the folder shape that is the reader's own. open_in.html substitutes the handle into the FOLDER and never into the name, which is the whole difference from `data-dsl-repo` above - and it is why a drop box offers the same `Edit online` / `Edit locally` as every other shape rather than nothing at all. Gated on `submit_path`, which is this shape's key and no other's: asking `submit_shape` again here would be a second spelling of the same question, and the two eventually disagree. `cutoff_sentence` and `late_rule` close the paragraph for every arm at once, which is why neither is inside the `case`: a sentence repeated per arm is a sentence three arms keep in step, and the first reword of it left one of them saying something else. The cutoff text is written in Python (`course.CUTOFF_SENTENCE`), not here, because the About line of every submission repo says the same thing and the two are read minutes apart. `late_rule` (site.py, off the assignment's own grading_config.yml) closes the paragraph, so what happens after the deadline is read where the deadline's own answer is. Written for every TIMED shape and for no other: `external` collects no commits, so no day is counted and no penalty is ever applied (`course.collects_commits`), and a sentence there would quote a rule about a deadline this toolkit does not hold. The theme reads the KEY's presence rather than asking the shape again - a second spelling of "which shapes are timed" is one that eventually disagrees with the first. {%- endcomment -%} {% unless page.handout_pending %} {% if page.submit_shape == "external" %}
